text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Monday.

LONDON - Shares greeted the long-awaited announcement of the country's election date with little excitement, looking instead to Wall Street for direction and closing lower as the Dow tumbled. The FTSE 100 index lost 51 points to 4,373.3.
FRANKFURT - Shares closed slightly lower, with the DAX-30 index of leading German shares off 8.30 points to 3,350.99.

PARIS - Stocks finished sharply lower, mirroring falls in the dollar and bond prices due to worries that U.S. interest rates may be headed higher. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 57.24 points, or 2.16 percent, at 2,588.38.

ZURICH - A weaker dollar in European trading and widespread insecurity about the U.S. and European interest rate developments soured sentiment, and the all-share Swiss Performance Index fell 42.02 points, or 1.43 percent, to 2,891.84.
TOKYO - Stocks ended higher after clawing back late in the session but investors' enthusiasm was still muted, brokers said. The Nikkei 225 rose 129.86 points to 18,053.50.
HONG KONG - A rebound in the property sector swept stocks to a firm close after heavy losses last week. The Hang Seng Index added 102 points, or 0.80 percent, to 12,838.53.

SYDNEY - Political instability in Papua New Guinea hit the shares of companies with links to that country but the overall market, particularly banks, closed firm after a bounce on Wall Street. The All Ordinaries index rose 4.2 points to 2,427.4.
